question: A 60-year-old man with a 1-year history of recurrent aspiration pneumonia is brought to the emergency department by his daughter after being found unconscious and gasping for air in his bed. Despite resuscitative efforts, the patient dies. Autopsy of the patient shows degeneration of the corticospinal tracts and anterior horn cells of the upper cervical cord. There is asymmetrical atrophy of the limb muscles, the diaphragm, and the intercostal muscles. Which of the following drugs would have most likely slowed the progression of this patient's condition?
reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Degeneration of corticospinal tracts and anterior horn cells of the upper cervical cord" -> "Asymmetrical atrophy of limb muscles, diaphragm, and intercostal muscles" -> "Motor neuron disease (MND) likely Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS)" -> "Progressive muscle weakness and respiratory failure" -> "Need for a drug that slows disease progression in ALS" -> 70%

CHAIN: "Degeneration of corticospinal tracts and anterior horn cells of the upper cervical cord" -> "Asymmetrical atrophy of limb muscles, diaphragm, and intercostal muscles" -> "Motor neuron disease (MND)" -> "Riluzole is the only FDA-approved drug for ALS that has shown to slow disease progression" -> 80%
analysis: The patient's presentation with degeneration of corticospinal tracts and anterior horn cells, along with muscle atrophy, suggests a diagnosis of Amyotrophic Lateral Sclerosis (ALS). The drug that has shown to slow the progression of ALS is Riluzole.
